text:
elaine: Heads up — saw inconsistent SSE parsing in node-sdk v0.13.2. Final chunk sometimes gets dropped when client disconnects fast or proxy returns 499. Repro below, looking for parity notes and quick mitigations. :eyes:
kevin: Can you paste a minimal repro and logs? Is this only Node or Python too?
elaine: Minimal repro: spin up a simple fetch stream and abort after ~200ms. Sometimes the last JSON object never gets emitted because our parser waits for newline. Example:
```js
const res = await fetch(url, { signal });
const rl = createInterface({ input: res.body });
rl.on('line', line => parser.push(line));
res.body.on('end', () => parser.flush());
signal.abort(200);
```
If the connection ends mid-line (no trailing "\n"), current code ignores the fragment until next newline -> lost final token.
sophie: Python SDK was doing a flush-on-close, which is why we haven't seen it as much there. Node's stream "end" vs "close" vs "aborted" semantics are messy. Also some proxies terminate with HTTP 499 which doesn't include a clean final chunk.
jean: (ci-bot) I saw one flaky test in our integration suite that timed out parsing the final response last week, maybe related. Link: https://ci.internal/12345 :warning:
juan: Suggestion: on any termination event (end/close/aborted/response-abort) we should attempt to parse remaining buffer as a final chunk — not require a trailing newline. That should be safe because model outputs are JSON-like with boundaries.
kevin: Agree. Quick patch: in the SSE parser, when stream emits 'end' or emits an error, call _consumeBuffer(true) which treats remainder as terminated. Also add a short debounce so transient socket closes don't double-emit. I'll open PR. :bug:
elaine: Also found a proxy-specific quirk — nginx with proxy_buffering off will split chunks differently; tests should simulate split bytes mid-json. Can we add an integration test that injects partial chunks (e.g., split object across two data events) and then terminate connection?
sophie: I'll add a Python-based harness that can simulate: send "data: {\"text\": \"hello" then wait 50ms then " world\"}\n\n" then close with 499. We should assert Node/Python SDKs both emit same final message.
kevin: Plan: 1) Add unit tests for parser to accept final fragment, 2) integration test with nginx-like splitter and 499, 3) backport patch to 0.13.x, 4) add a sample app in /examples that demonstrates robust client-side handling. I'll assign to myself and ping when PR ready.
elaine: For immediate mitigation, apps can wrap stream handling with a timeout and on abort call parser.flush() manually. Example API we can expose: sdk.stream({ onChunk }) returns object with .flush() method. We should document this in the SDK migration guide.
jean: (ci-bot) Build queued for branch fix/sse-final-fragment — job 9876.
juan: Also note SDK parity: update the SDK parity matrix to mark this behavior as fixed only after both Py/Node tests pass. I'll file the dx ticket.
kevin: Thanks — will include tests and changelog entry. ETA EOD tomorrow for draft PR. :white_check_mark:
